thread:
Priya (support): Hey team, DataCo is seeing p95/p99 spikes for requests that use function-calling + JSON schema validation. Reported API p95 jumped from ~120ms to ~420ms in the last 4 hours. They escalated. Anyone seen similar?
Ethan (eng-runtime): Noted. Any request IDs or example payloads from DataCo? Tool-calling paths can add overhead if schema validation runs synchronously for every call.
DataCo (customer): @Priya attaching a small sample and a trace link: https://traces.redwood/example/trace-abc123. The slow ones are when our app triggers the tool router to call an external retriever.
Priya (support): Paste of the header we got from their trace: "router_time_ms": 310, "schema_validation_ms": 45, "model_infer_ms": 60, "sdk_overhead_ms": 5. Looks like router_time is the big chunk.
Marta (eng-platform): Hmm router_time 310ms is heavy. That includes routing decision + tool dispatch + syncing responses. Any config changes on their side? New schema pushed?
DataCo (customer): We recently started sending a stricter JSON schema for function outputs to enforce more rigorous validation. No other app changes.
Ethan (eng-runtime): That aligns. Current router flow validates the tool output against the schema synchronously before returning to the user. For large outputs or nested arrays that can add noticeable time, and it blocks the KV cache path.
Kai (oncall): I pulled infra metrics — during the spike we had a surge of ~2.3x concurrent tool-router tasks on the hosted pool. Router worker queue depth increased and some workers got CPU-throttled on decoding/validation.
Priya (support): Customer is asking for quick mitigations to reduce p95 now, while we investigate root cause. Suggestions?
Ethan (eng-runtime): Short term options: 1) Turn off strict schema validation for the customer's route (feature-flag) 2) Switch tool-calls to async mode if their client can accept streaming/followups 3) Route their traffic to a dedicated router pool with higher concurrency.
Marta (eng-platform): We can flip a per-customer flag to disable validation in <10 minutes. But warn DataCo about potential malformed tool outputs. We could also apply a temporary model-routing policy to use a lighter-weight tool-runner.
DataCo (customer): We need the p95 under 200ms or our SLAs are violated. Disabling validation would be acceptable short-term. Can you do it now?
Priya (support): @Marta can you schedule the feature-flag?
Marta (eng-platform): I'll roll the flag for customer:dataco now. deploy-bot: starting rollout of feature-flag disable-schema-validation for customer=dataco.
deploy-bot: rollout started — step 1/3 applied to 20% of routes.
Marta (eng-platform): Applying to remaining nodes... deploy-bot: rollout 100% complete.
deploy-bot: rollout finished — feature-flag disable-schema-validation for customer=dataco is now ON.
Priya (support): DataCo, can you retry a few of the failing requests and post updated p95/p99?
DataCo (customer): Re-ran a test set. New numbers: p95 ~180ms, p99 ~320ms. Big improvement on p95, p99 still spiky. Thanks.
Ethan (eng-runtime): Good. p99 still high likely due to router queueing at peak concurrency or a few large payloads. We should check if some tool calls return huge payloads that make validation expensive even when disabled (e.g., post-processing still happening).
Kai (oncall): Checking traces for the p99 tails: several show long GC pauses on router workers and one long S3 fetch for tool enrichment (2s). So a combination of infra jitter + external tool latency.
Priya (support): Action list for root cause: 1) Ethan to instrument per-tool output size and validation time split 2) Marta to provision a temporary dedicated router pool for dataco traffic 3) Kai to add alert if router queue depth > threshold 4) Support to coordinate with DataCo about reducing max returned tokens.
Ethan (eng-runtime): I'll add fine-grained metrics: tool.router.validation_ms, tool.router.dispatch_ms, tool.output_bytes. ETA ~2 hours for metrics + dashboard. I'll also spike a code path to do schema validation off the critical path (async validation with best-effort warnings) — that's longer term.
Marta (eng-platform): I'll create a dedicated router pool with +30% cpu and larger worker count and route dataco to it. ETA 20 minutes.
Kai (oncall): I'll tune the queue alert thresholds and add a temporary suppression for minor alerts during the mitigation.
DataCo (customer): Appreciate it. Also, can you document best practices for schema size and tool output limits? We want to avoid repeated escalations.
Priya (support): Yes — we'll send a short doc: recommended max output size, use pagination, prefer streaming where possible, and opt-in to async validation.
Ethan (eng-runtime): Follow-up plan: 1) Implement non-blocking schema validation (configurable per-route) 2) Add a lightweight JSON-schema preflight that only checks shape instead of full validation 3) Improve tool-router scheduling to prioritize small/streaming calls. I'll open a ticket with proposed design.
Marta (eng-platform): After dedicated pool is live, we'll monitor p95/p99 and decide whether to keep it or auto-scale router pools differently.
Priya (support): For transparency I'll update DataCo once the dedicated pool is live and then again when we have the async validation design.
DataCo (customer): Dedicated pool is live and tests look good — p95 ~150ms, p99 ~210ms. We'll accept that for now. Thanks for quick turnaround.
Kai (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated for now. We'll continue to monitor.
Priya (support): Closing loop — next steps summarized in the follow-up ticket. Thanks everyone. :white_check_mark:
Ethan (eng-runtime): I'll paste the ticket link once created.
Priya (support): Ticket link: https://issues.redwood/INFR-4821 — contains metrics, traces, and next-step owners.
